en: The Sutra Spoken by the Buddha on Contemplating Bodhisattva Maitreya’s Ascent to Be Born in Tuṣita Heaven, translated by the Song dynasty layman Juqu Jingsheng.
Thus have I heard: At one time, the Buddha was staying at Śrāvastī in the Jeta Grove, Anāthapiṇḍada’s Park.

At that time, during the first watch of the night, the World-Honored One emitted golden light from his entire body. This light circled the Jeta Grove seven times, illuminating Sudatta’s house so that it also became golden. There was a golden light like a mass of clouds, and throughout the kingdom of Śrāvastī, golden lotus flowers rained down everywhere. Within that radiance were immeasurable hundreds of thousands of great transformation Buddhas, all of whom proclaimed these words:
"Now, within this assembly, there are a thousand bodhisattvas; the first to attain Buddhahood shall be named Krakucchanda, and the last to attain Buddhahood shall be named Ruci."
When these words had been spoken, the Venerable Ājñātakauṇḍinya rose from his meditation together with his retinue of two hundred and fifty people;
the Venerable Mahākāśyapa, together with his retinue of two hundred and fifty people;
and the Venerable Mahāmaudgalyāyana, together with his retinue of two hundred and fifty people.
The Venerable Śāriputra was accompanied by his retinue of two hundred and fifty persons;
the Bhikṣuṇī Mahāprajāpatī was accompanied by her retinue of one thousand bhikṣuṇīs;
and the Elder Sudatta was accompanied by three thousand upāsakas.
Vishakha-mātā was present together with two thousand upāsikās;
furthermore, there was the bodhisattva mahāsattva named Bhadrapāla, who was accompanied by his retinue of sixteen bodhisattvas;
and Mañjuśrī, the Dharma Prince, was accompanied by his retinue of five hundred bodhisattvas.
The entire great assembly—devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, and others—beheld the Buddha’s radiance and gathered like clouds.

At that time, the World-Honored One extended his broad and long tongue, emitting a thousand rays of light; each ray possessed a thousand colors, and within each color were immeasurable transformation buddhas.

These emanated Buddhas, with one voice and in unison, all expounded the dhāraṇī methods of the pure great bodhisattvas—profound and inconceivable—which are as follows: the Ānandamukha Dhāraṇī, the Śūnyatājñāna Dhāraṇī, the Asaṅgasvabhāva Dhāraṇī, and the Mahāvimokṣa-nimitta Dhāraṇī.
At that time, the World-Honored One, with a single voice, expounded ten billion dharani-gates.

Having spoken these dharanis, there was a bodhisattva in the assembly named Maitreya who, upon hearing what the Buddha had said, immediately attained ten million billion dharani-gates. He rose from his seat, adjusted his robes, and stood before the Buddha with palms joined in reverence.
At that time, Upāli also rose from his seat, prostrated himself with his head at the Buddha’s feet, and addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!

In the past, within the Vinaya and the various scriptural collections (*sūtra-piṭaka*), the World-Honored One declared that Ajita shall become a Buddha in the future. This Ajita still possesses the body of an ordinary person (*pṛthagjana*) and has not yet severed the outflows (*āsrava*). Where will this person be reborn when his life comes to an end?”

Although this person has now left the household life, they do not cultivate meditative concentration nor sever their afflictions; yet the Buddha has prophesied that this person will undoubtedly attain Buddhahood—where will this person be reborn at the end of their life?
The Buddha told Upāli:
“Listen attentively, listen attentively, and reflect upon this well.
The Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha now proclaims in this assembly the prediction of Anuttarā Samyaksaṃbodhi for the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Maitreya.”
"This person, twelve years from now, will at the end of his life surely attain rebirth in the Tuṣita Heaven.

At that time, there will be five hundred trillion devaputras in the Tuṣita Heaven; each and every devaputra shall practice the profound dānapāramitā. For the sake of making offerings to the Bodhisattva who is in his last birth before Buddhahood (ekajātipratibaddha), they will use the power of their celestial merit to construct palaces. Each will remove their sandalwood and maṇi-jewel crowns, kneel with palms joined, and make this vow, saying:"

"I now hold this priceless jewel and celestial crown to make an offering to this being of great resolve; for before long, this person shall attain Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi in a future life. May my precious crown transform into ritual offerings whenever I receive the prediction of enlightenment under that Buddha within his adorned realm."
In this manner, each of those devaputras knelt with their right knees on the ground and made great vows, just as [the Buddha] had done.
When the devaputras had finished making these vows, those jeweled crowns transformed into five hundred myriads of koṭis of jeweled palaces.
Each jeweled palace had seven layers of walls, and each wall was composed of the seven precious substances.
Each jewel emits five hundred billion rays of light; within each ray of light are five hundred billion lotus flowers;
each lotus flower transforms into five hundred billion rows of trees made of the seven treasures;
each leaf of every tree has five hundred billion precious colors; and within each precious color are five hundred billion rays of Jāmbūnada gold light.
From within each ray of Jāmbūnada gold light emerged five hundred billion celestial jewel-women;
each jewel-woman stood beneath a tree, holding ten billion jewels and countless necklaces, producing exquisite music.
Within the sounds of this music, they expounded the practice of the Dharma-wheel of the stage of non-retrogression.

The trees produce fruit the color of crystal; all colors enter into this crystal hue. From these lights, which swirl and turn to the right, flow forth various sounds, and these sounds expound the Dharma of great loving-kindness and great compassion.

Each wall was sixty-two *yojanas* high and fourteen *yojanas* thick; five hundred billion dragon kings surrounded these walls, and each dragon king rained down five hundred billion rows of trees made of the seven treasures, adorning the tops of the walls.
Naturally, the wind blows and stirs these trees; as the trees rub against one another, they proclaim suffering, emptiness, impermanence, non-self, and the various pāramitās.
“At that time, there was a great deity in this palace named Lohitākṣa (Lao-du-bo-ti). He immediately rose from his seat, paid homage to the Buddhas of the ten directions, and made a vast vow:
‘If my merit is such that it should provide for the construction of the Hall of Good Dharma for Maitreya Bodhisattva, may a pearl spontaneously emerge from the forehead of my head.’”

Having made this vow, five hundred billion precious jewels spontaneously emerged from his forehead; they were composed of lapis lazuli, crystal, and every variety of color, all perfectly complete, like purple-blue *maṇi* gems, transparent throughout both inside and out.
This mani-light revolved in the air, transforming into forty-nine tiers of subtle and wondrous jewel palaces; each and every balustrade was composed of ten trillion Brahma-mani jewels.

Within the various railings, nine hundred million devaputras and five hundred billion devakanyās were spontaneously manifested. From the hands of each devaputra, there were manifested immeasurable billions of lotus flowers made of the seven precious gems; upon each lotus flower were immeasurable billions of rays of light, and within those lights were present all kinds of musical instruments.

Thus, the celestial music played spontaneously without being struck; when these sounds emerged, the goddesses naturally took up various musical instruments and vied with one another to rise and dance and sing.
The melodies they chanted expounded upon the ten wholesome deeds and the four great vows, and all the devas who heard them conceived the aspiration for supreme enlightenment.

“At that time, within the gardens there were channels of eight-colored lapis lazuli; each channel was constructed from five hundred billion precious jewels, and within each channel flowed water of eight flavors, complete with the eight colors.”

The water surged upward, flowing between the beams and rafters, and outside the four gates it miraculously produced four flowers; as the water emerged from within the flowers, it was like a stream of precious blossoms.

Upon each flower were twenty-four celestial maidens, their complexions subtle and wondrous, with bodily features adorned like those of Bodhisattvas. In their hands, five billion precious vessels spontaneously appeared; within each vessel, the various nectars of the heavens naturally filled them to the brim. Adorned on their left shoulders with immeasurable necklaces and carrying immeasurable musical instruments upon their right shoulders, they remained like clouds in the sky as they emerged from the water, praising the Bodhisattva’s six *pāramitās*.
Should anyone be reborn in the Tuṣita Heaven, they will naturally obtain these celestial maidens as attendants.

There were also great lion thrones made of the seven treasures, four yojanas in height, adorned with Jāmbūnada gold and immeasurable varieties of jewels. At each of the four corners of the thrones grew four lotus flowers; each lotus was composed of a hundred jewels, and from each jewel issued ten billion rays of light.
That light was subtle and wondrous; it transformed into five hundred billion clusters of various precious flowers, adorning the jeweled canopy.
At that time, the hundreds of thousands of Brahma Kings from the ten directions each held a wondrous jewel of the Brahma heavens, using them as jeweled bells suspended above the jeweled canopy.
At that time, the minor Brahmā King took divine jewels and fashioned them into a net that completely covered the canopy above.
Then, hundreds of thousands of countless sons and daughters of gods, along with their retinues, each held precious flowers and scattered them upon the seats.
From these lotus flowers, five hundred billion precious women naturally emerged, each holding a white fly-whisk and standing in attendance within the pavilion.
At the four corners of the palace were four jeweled pillars; upon each jeweled pillar were hundreds of thousands of multi-storied pavilions, draped and entwined with Brahma-maṇi jewels.

At that time, within the various pavilions there were hundreds of thousands of celestial maidens of incomparable beauty, holding musical instruments in their hands. From the sounds of these instruments, they proclaimed suffering, emptiness, impermanence, non-self, and the various *pāramitās*.
Thus, this celestial palace possessed billions of immeasurable jewel colors, and each of the maidens likewise shared the same jewel color.
At that time, immeasurable devas from the ten directions reached the end of their lives and all made the vow to be reborn in the Tuṣita Heaven Palace.
At that time, there were five great deities in the Tuṣita Heaven Palace:

the first great deity was named Ratnaketu (Jewel Banner). From his body, he rained down the seven treasures, scattering them within the palace walls; each jewel transformed into immeasurable musical instruments, suspended in mid-air and sounding spontaneously without being struck, producing immeasurable melodies that accorded with the inclinations of the beings' minds.

The second great deity is named Flower Virtue (*Puṣpadeva*). From his body, he rains down various flowers that completely cover the palace walls, transforming into flower canopies. Each individual flower canopy is preceded by hundreds of thousands of banners and streamers. The third great deity is named Fragrant Sound (*Gandharva*).

From the pores of his body, he rains down the exquisite "this-side-of-the-ocean" sandalwood incense; this fragrance is like clouds, appearing in the colors of a hundred jewels as it circles the palace seven times.

The fourth great deity is named Joyful Delight (*Nandirata*). He rains down wish-fulfilling jewels (*cintāmaṇi*); each jewel naturally comes to rest atop the banners and streamers, clearly proclaiming the immeasurable taking of refuge in the Buddha, the Dharma, and the Sangha of Bhikṣus, as well as preaching the five precepts, immeasurable wholesome dharmas, and the various *pāramitās*, benefiting and encouraging those with the aspiration for Bodhi.

The fifth great deity is named Right Sound; from all the pores of his body flow various waters, upon each of which are five hundred billion flowers. Upon each flower are twenty-five jade maidens, and from every pore of each jade maiden’s body emerge all manner of sounds, surpassing the music of even the Queen of the Heavenly Demons.
The Buddha told Upāli:
"This is called Tuṣita Heaven, a place of supreme and wondrous merit that is the retribution for the ten wholesome paths of action.

If I were to remain in the world for a small kalpa and speak extensively on the retributions of bodhisattvas in their final birth before succession (ekajātipratibaddha) as well as the fruits of the ten wholesome paths, I could not exhaustively describe them; therefore, I shall now explain them briefly for you."
The Buddha told Upāli:

"If there are bhikṣus or any of the great assembly who do not weary of birth and death but delight in being born in the heavens; who cherish and revere the unsurpassed mind of enlightenment (bodhicitta); and who desire to become disciples of Maitreya—these should perform this contemplation."

One who practices this contemplation should observe the five precepts, the eightfold fast, and the full set of monastic precepts; with body and mind diligent, they should not seek the severance of fetters, but instead cultivate the ten wholesome dharmas. They should contemplate, one by one, the supreme and wondrous bliss of the Tuṣita Heaven. One who practices this contemplation is said to practice right contemplation; any other contemplation is called wrong contemplation.
At that time, Upāli rose from his seat, adjusted his robes, prostrated with his head at the Buddha’s feet, and addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
There are such supremely wonderful and joyful matters in the Tuṣita Heaven. When will this Great Being pass away from Jambudvīpa and be reborn in that heaven?”
The Buddha told Upāli:

"Maitreya was previously born in the village of Kapilavastu in the kingdom of Vārāṇasī, in the family of the great Brahmin Pāpali. Twelve years hence, on the fifteenth day of the second month, he will return to his place of birth and sit cross-legged as if entering the meditative absorption of final extinction."
His body was the color of purple-gold, its radiance brilliant and dazzling like that of hundreds of thousands of suns, extending upward as far as the Tuṣita Heaven.

His physical relics were like cast golden images, neither moving nor shaking; within the halo surrounding his body, the characters and meanings of the Śūraṅgama Samādhi Prajñāpāramitā shone forth with vivid clarity.
At that time, all the humans and devas immediately erected a magnificent stupa made of various jewels to make offerings to the śarīra.

Then, within the mani palace of the seven-jeweled terrace in Tuṣita Heaven, a lion throne suddenly manifested by transformation; upon it, he sat cross-legged atop a lotus flower. His body was the color of Jāmbūnada gold, sixteen yojanas in height, and fully endowed with the thirty-two marks and eighty minor characteristics. The hair of his uṣṇīṣa on the crown of his head was the color of deep blue lapis lazuli, and his celestial crown was adorned with Śakrābhilagna mani jewels and hundreds of thousands of millions of kinnuka gems.

That celestial jewel crown possessed hundreds of billions of colors; within each color were immeasurable hundreds of thousands of transformation Buddhas, with various transformation Bodhisattvas serving as their attendants.
Furthermore, great Bodhisattvas from other directions performed the eighteen transformations, dwelling freely and at will within the crown.

Between Maitreya’s eyebrows is the mark of the white tuft (*ūrṇā-kośa*), from which flows forth a multitude of rays of light in the colors of a hundred jewels. Among his thirty-two marks, each individual mark contains five hundred *koṭis* of jewel colors; likewise, each secondary mark (*anuvyañjana*) also contains five hundred *koṭis* of jewel colors. From each mark and secondary mark, there brilliantly issues eighty-four thousand clouds of radiant light.

Together with the various sons of heaven, he sits upon flower thrones, and throughout the six periods of day and night, he constantly preaches the practice of the Dharma-wheel of the stage of non-retrogression (*avaivartika-bhūmi*).
Within a single period, he brings to fulfillment five hundred *koṭis* of sons of heaven, causing them not to retrogress from *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
Thus, while dwelling in the Tuṣita Heaven, he constantly preaches this Dharma day and night to deliver the various devaputras.
After fifty-six billion years according to the reckoning of Jambudvīpa, he will then descend to be born in Jambudvīpa, as described in the *Maitreya’s Descent into the World Sūtra*.
The Buddha told Upāli:
“This is called the cause and condition for Maitreya Bodhisattva’s passing away from Jambudvīpa and being reborn in Tuṣita Heaven.

After the Buddha’s parinirvāṇa, if among my disciples there are those who diligently cultivate all merits, whose majestic deportment is unimpaired, who sweep stupas and smear the ground with plaster, who offer various famous incenses and exquisite flowers, who practice various samādhis and enter deeply into right concentration (*samāpatti*), and who read and recite the sūtras—such persons should, with a sincere heart, even if they have not yet severed their fetters, act as if they have attained the six supernatural powers (*abhijñā*). They should maintain constant mindfulness and recollect the image of the Buddha, and invoke the name of Maitreya.”

If such persons as these, for even the duration of a single thought-moment, receive the eight precepts and fast, cultivate various pure deeds, and give rise to great vows, then after the end of their lives—just as a strong man might flex or extend his arm—they shall immediately attain rebirth in the Tuṣita Heaven. There, they will sit cross-legged upon lotus flowers while hundreds of thousands of devaputras perform celestial music and scatter heavenly *māndārava* and *mahāmāndārava* flowers over them, praising them, saying:
"Excellent! Excellent!"
"Noble son! You have extensively cultivated meritorious deeds in Jambudvīpa and have been reborn here.
This place is named Tuṣita Heaven, and the current Lord of this realm is named Maitreya; you should take refuge in him."

At these words, he immediately prostrated; having finished his prostration, he gazed intently at the light of the white tuft of hair between the Buddha’s brows and instantly attained transcendence from the sins of birth and death for ninety billion kalpas.

At that time, the Bodhisattva, in accordance with their past affinities, expounds the sublime Dharma for them, causing them to become firm and non-regressive in their resolve for the unsurpassed path.

Such sentient beings, if they purify all karma and practice the six dharmas, will certainly and without doubt be reborn in the Tuṣita Heaven to meet Maitreya; they will also descend to Jambudvīpa together with Maitreya, being the first to hear the Dharma. In future ages, they will encounter all the Buddhas of the Bhadrakalpa, and during the Nakṣatraprabhāsa Kalpa, they will likewise encounter the various Buddha-Bhagavats, receiving the prediction of enlightenment (bodhi-vyākaraṇa) in the presence of those Buddhas.
The Buddha told Upāli:

"After the Buddha’s parinirvāṇa, if there are bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, upāsikās, or among the great assembly of devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, and others, who hear the name of the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Maitreya, and having heard it, rejoice and pay him respectful homage and prostrations—such a person, at the end of life, shall attain rebirth in that realm in the time it takes to snap one's fingers, no different from what was described before.

Moreover, anyone who merely hears this name of Maitreya will, at the end of life, not fall into dark places, borderlands, wrong views, or various evil disciplines; they will always be born with right view, be endowed with a virtuous retinue, and never slander the Triple Gem."
The Buddha told Upāli:

“If a son of good family or a daughter of good family has violated various prohibitions and committed manifold evil deeds, yet hears the name of this Bodhisattva’s great compassion and prostrates with their five limbs on the ground, repenting with a sincere heart, all these evil karmas will quickly be purified.”

In future ages, when sentient beings hear the name of this Bodhisattva’s great compassion, they shall fashion his image and offer incense, flowers, robes, silk canopies, banners, and streamers, prostrating before it with focused mindfulness. When such a person is about to die, Maitreya Bodhisattva will emit from the white tuft between his eyebrows the light of the mark of a Great Man, and together with the sons of heaven, he will rain down *mandārava* flowers to come and welcome that person.

This person shall immediately attain rebirth in that land; there they will encounter Maitreya, prostrate themselves before him in reverence, and before their heads have even been raised, they will hear the Dharma. They will then attain non-retrogression from the Unsurpassed Way and, in future ages, encounter Buddhas and Tathāgatas as numerous as the sands of the Ganges.
The Buddha told Upāli: "Listen attentively now;
this Bodhisattva Maitreya shall, in a future age, act as a great place of refuge for sentient beings."
If there are those who take refuge in Maitreya Bodhisattva, you should know that such persons shall attain non-retrogression from the unsurpassed path.
When Maitreya Bodhisattva becomes a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, these practitioners, upon seeing the Buddha’s radiance, will immediately receive their prediction of enlightenment.
The Buddha told Upāli:

“After the Buddha’s parinirvāṇa, if any among the fourfold assembly of disciples, devas, nāgas, or spirits, should wish to be born in the Tuṣita Heaven, they should perform this contemplation, binding their mindfulness in reflection. They should keep the Tuṣita Heaven in mind, uphold the Buddha’s prohibitory precepts for one day up to seven days, contemplate the ten wholesome actions and practice the path of the ten wholesome deeds. Those who dedicate these merits with the vow to be born before Maitreya should perform this contemplation.”

For one who practices this contemplation, if they see a single celestial being or a single lotus flower, or if for even a single thought-moment they invoke the name of Maitreya, that person shall eliminate the karmic offenses of birth and death accumulated over twelve hundred kalpas;
if they merely hear the name of Maitreya and join their palms in reverent worship, that person shall eliminate the karmic offenses of birth and death accumulated over fifty kalpas;
and if there are those who pay homage to Maitreya, they shall eliminate the karmic offenses of birth and death accumulated over ten billion kalpas.
"Even if you are not born in the heavens, in a future age you shall likewise encounter him beneath the Dragon Flower Bodhi tree and resolve upon the unsurpassed mind.

When these words were spoken, an immeasurable multitude rose from their seats, prostrated at the feet of the Buddha, and prostrated at the feet of Maitreya; they then circumambulated the Buddha and the Bodhisattva Maitreya a hundred thousand times.
Those who had not yet attained the Way each made a vow:

"We, the eight classes of devas and humans, now before the Buddha make this sincere and truthful vow: in a future age, upon meeting Maitreya and casting off these bodies, may we all attain rebirth in the Tuṣita Heaven."
The World-Honored One gave this prediction:
"You and all others in future ages who cultivate merit and uphold the precepts shall all be reborn before Maitreya Bodhisattva and be received into his care."
The Buddha told Upāli:
"One who practices this contemplation is said to practice correctly; one who contemplates otherwise is said to practice erroneously.
At that time, the Venerable Ānanda rose from his seat, joined his palms, knelt with his right knee on the ground, and addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
Excellent, World-Honored One!

You have eloquently spoken of all the merits possessed by Maitreya, and you have also prophesied the fruits and rewards obtained by sentient beings who cultivate merit in future ages; I now rejoice in this.”
"So be it, World-Honored One!
How should this essential Dharma be received and upheld?
What should this sutra be named?"
The Buddha told Ānanda:

"Uphold these words of the Buddha and be careful not to forget or lose them; for the sake of future generations, open the path to rebirth in the heavens and reveal the signs of Bodhi, so that the lineage of the Buddhas shall not be severed."

This sutra is titled "The Parinirvāṇa of Maitreya Bodhisattva," and it is also titled "Contemplating Maitreya Bodhisattva’s Birth in Tuṣita Heaven and Exhorting the Arising of the Bodhicitta"; thus should it be upheld.
When the Buddha spoke these words, one hundred thousand bodhisattvas who had gathered from other directions attained the Śūraṅgama Samādhi;
eighty trillion devas resolved their minds on Bodhi, all vowing to follow Maitreya in his descent to be born in this world.

When the Buddha had spoken these words, the fourfold assembly, the devas, nāgas, and the eight classes of supernatural beings, having heard what the Buddha taught, were all greatly rejoiced; they paid homage to the Buddha and withdrew.
The Sutra Spoken by the Buddha on the Visualization of Bodhisattva Maitreya’s Rebirth in the Tuṣita Heaven.
